transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2028-01-17 15:00 UTC
Duration: 47 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel, Ethan Kim, Sofia Alvarez (Redwood) / Aria Chen, Liam O'Neill, Priya Rao, Noah Becker (BlueForge)

Summary: initial qualify focused on where to host embeddings + rerank stack. BlueForge is evaluating hosted vs dedicated vs private (VPC) for a hybrid retrieval + rerank product; main concerns are throughput (QPS), embedding dimensionality impact, tail latency and fallback to smaller models when capacity spikes. 

Topics: current vector DB, embed dims, batching, quantization, VPC/KMS/SOC2, pilot success criteria, cost targets, benchmarking next steps.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya: hey everyone thanks for joining um we'll kick off, this is Maya from Redwood, i have Ethan and Sofia with me from SE. quick intro then we'll jump into your stack.
[00:08] Aria: hi yeah Aria here head of search at BlueForge, thanks for doing this. we want to figure out hosting and rerank integration, we have an internal vector DB today but it's brittle with load.
[00:16] Ethan: great, quick Q — what are your target p95 and p99 on production queries and what QPS are we talking about?
[00:22] Priya: right now our tail is rough, p95 ~120ms p99 around 420ms, that includes DB fanout + a small rerank L2. peak QPS is 220 but sustained 60 to 80.
[00:34] Ethan: ok that gives us something to size. are your embeddings 1536 or larger? dims matter a lot for host memory and sharding.
[00:41] Priya: primary model is 1536, we also have a 1024 variant for mobile. most vectors stored in our Milvus cluster, indexed HNSW, disk-backed shards.
[00:50] Liam: and we are considering moving to private colocation or dedicated GPUs cause we're seeing noisy neighbors on cloud infra, so latency spikes at peak.
[01:00] Maya: yeah that maps to two common paths — 1) Redwood hosted with autoscaling + fallback to smaller model variants, and prefix caching for hot queries; 2) Dedicated pools you reserve for consistent throughput; 3) Private (VPC / on-prem) if you need network isolation and KMS control.
[01:18] Aria: our security team cares about KMS and audit logs, SOC2 is a must. can you do SAML SSO and per-route audit tracing?
[01:26] Sofia: yes SOC2 + SAML are supported, we can provide audit log retention options and you can push logs to your SIEM. for VPC/private we have options for customer-managed KMS or HSM integration.
[01:36] Noah: what's the cost delta between hosted and dedicated? ballpark per-token or per-embedding unit?
[01:41] Maya: ballpark — hosted is easiest for start, cost per-embedding call lower at low volume but dedicated reserves GPU capacity which drops unit cost at scale. we'll include a cost model in the doc.
[01:52] Priya: re: rerank, we do a top-200 fanout from VDB then rerank with a 13B model; that's the expensive hop. could Redwood rerank on the same infra?
[02:02] Ethan: yes you can co-locate rerank on GPU pools. common pattern is do vector fanout from your VDB to a small lightweight embed-based filter then rerank on a quantized model or 8-bit variant to save cost. Also we support automatic fallback: if large model latency would violate SLO, route to a smaller model.
[02:20] Aria: the fanout time from the DB is our pain point, HNSW sometimes has cold shard hits. any caching options?
[02:27] Sofia: Redwood supports prefix/KV caching for repeated queries and can cache top-k results, also we can do hybrid search where a dense embed score is combined with a lightweight BM25 layer to reduce fanout. might cut p99 substantially.
[02:42] Liam: what's the integration pattern for Milvus? we prefer to continue with what we have not rip and replace.
[02:47] Ethan: integration is usually via the Redwood SDK returning embedding vectors or IDs, then your VDB does nearest neighbor and returns top candidates which are sent back to Redwood's rerank endpoints. Alternatively we can host embeddings inside Redwood and call out to your VDB for hybrid recall. so two patterns: send vectors out for scoring or serve embeddings from Redwood.
[03:05] Priya: hmm we worry about vector replication and consistency if we serve from Redwood. are there sync guarantees?
[03:10] Sofia: sync is a policy you choose — streaming updates, periodic batch refresh, or push-based webhook. for strict consistency we'd recommend private/dedicated with colocated index or routing to your on-prem VDB over a private link.
[03:23] Aria: curious about dimension trade-offs. is 1536 much worse than 1024 for memory and latency?
[03:29] Ethan: yes 1536 is heavier — batch sizes drop, memory per vector is higher, and sharding counts increase. but if 1536 gives materially better relevance you can quantize to 16-bit or use product quantization (PQ) to reduce index size; Redwood Optimize can recommend quantization profiles per workload.
[03:46] Priya: we ran a quantization test and saw a small drop in recall on long-tail queries, tradeoff analysis would help.
[03:52] Maya: we can run a quality/regression check tied to your prompt set — Redwood Optimize will flag quality dips when you change quantization or model.
[04:00] Noah: what about tail latency under cold cache? do you do grooming or shard hot-spotting avoidance?
[04:06] Ethan: runtime has hot-shard mitigation and active routing. plus we support gradual rollouts and automatic fallback to reduce error surface. we also offer sharded warm pools so cold-cold misses are minimized.
[04:18] Liam: for the POC, we want to run a week of synthetic load to confirm p95/p99 improvements and an A/B with our current stack. how doable?
[04:25] Maya: totally doable. typical POC: 1) we ingest a sample set and run a 1-week throughput test with your query mix, 2) we measure p95/p99 and cost, 3) run a quality eval. we'll include a template for query mix and an ingest checklist.
[04:39] Aria: procurement wants to see security docs and a baseline SLA.
[04:43] Sofia: we'll attach SOC2 report, our standard SLA, and options for higher retention on logs for compliance.
[04:49] Priya: any gotchas on private deployments? data egress, network perf?
[04:54] Ethan: private deployments require a brief network design review — egress and cross-zone latency can be factors. we typically do a network perf test in advance and recommend colocating VDB and rerank where possible.
[05:05] Aria: ok what are pilot success criteria — what should we agree to?
[05:09] Maya: success criteria we propose: 1) p95 reduced by 20-30% from your baseline; 2) p99 under 250ms for 95% of test windows; 3) rerank cost per 1k queries within your budget threshold; 4) no regressions in top-N relevance on holdout set.
[05:25] Priya: those look reasonable. we want an explicit rollback plan and canary thresholds too.
[05:30] Sofia: we'll drive the canary config — percent traffic, automatic rollback conditions (latency, error rate, quality regression).
[05:38] Liam: do you support per-route RBAC and telemetry to our Grafana?
[05:42] Sofia: yes per-route tokens + RBAC via SSO, and we can stream metrics to your Prometheus/Grafana stack.
[05:49] Aria: for the rerank model itself: do you have recommended quantized variants of 13B or do customers typically use a 7B quantized model?
[05:58] Ethan: depends on tolerance. common pattern: 7B quantized for 95/99-critical low-latency paths, 13B for higher-quality off-peak scoring. Redwood also allows fallback routing by SLO — if 13B would exceed latency we fall back to 7B.
[06:12] Noah: great. any references you can send — sample benchmark of embedding dims vs latency?
[06:16] Maya: yes we'll attach a dim/throughput benchmark, our cost model, SOC2, and a POC checklist.
[06:23] Aria: earlier you mentioned hybrid search; can you elaborate briefly on combining BM25 + dense?
[06:28] Ethan: sure — hybrid blends BM25 lexical scoring and dense embeddings, we use a weighted scoring transform. this reduces fanout by prefiltering with BM25 and reduces dependence on heavy nearest neighbor operations. it particularly helps tail latency for long-tailed queries.
[06:43] Priya: that sounds promising for our catalog where lots of tail queries exist.
[06:46] Liam: on integration friction: how much dev time typically for the VDB->rerank integration?
[06:51] Sofia: for our standard SDK path it's usually 2-3 engineering weeks to wire up ingest and hit rerank endpoints, shorter if you keep your DB in place and just call Redwood rerank.
[07:02] Aria: any compliance differences between hosted and dedicated?
[07:06] Maya: hosted is SOC2-compliant; dedicated gives more isolation and predictable performance but same compliance posture; private gives you the tightest control and KMS options. procurement may prefer dedicated or private depending on contract terms.
[07:18] Noah: are there examples of customers doing multi-region failover for rerank?
[07:22] Ethan: yes, we route by policy — canary to a secondary region, and automatic fallback to a lightly-quantized model in a different region if primary region is congested.
[07:33] Priya: ok this is helpful. next steps for us: we'll pull sample logs and queries and send them. we'll also prep an internal list of stakeholders for the POC.
[07:42] Maya: perfect — recap: we'll send pricing + pilot scope doc, attach security artifacts, and Ethan will schedule the technical deep dive/benchmark. you will send query distribution and latency histograms.
[07:53] Aria: sounds good thanks everyone.
[07:55] Noah: thanks, bye.

(End of recording - rough transcription, some words may be mis-transcribed)
